title: Starter templates
intro_p: Three starters ship inside the binary — no fetching, no discovery paths. @dogbed template <name>@ prints one to stdout so you copy it and own it. @--list@ (or a bare @dogbed template@) shows the names:
list_tr:
$ dogbed template --list
verdict	PR review verdict: blockers, nits, summary.
release-notes	Release notes: highlights, breaking, added, changed, fixed.
reading-note	Reading note: author, rating, quote, notes.
verdict_p: @verdict@ — a PR review verdict: blockers, nits, summary. Example data in @share/verdict.json@.
rn_p: @release-notes@ — release notes: highlights, breaking changes, added, changed, fixed, a changelog link. Every section is guarded with @{% if %}@ — empty data makes the section disappear.
note_p: @reading-note@ — a reading note: author, source link, rating, quote, notes. Everything but the title is optional.
round_p: The whole round trip — print a starter, render it with the document shell:
round_tr:
$ dogbed template release-notes > release-notes.knap $ dogbed render release-notes.knap -d share/release-notes.json --title 'dogbed 0.2.0' --css style.css dogbed 0.2.0

dogbed 0.2.0

0.2.0 — 2026-09-29

gotcha_p: One thing to know before filling in your own data: Textile converts @--@ in values to an em-dash — see the "document shell page":shell.html for the details and the @…@ workaround.
